_readme: Seven kinds of activity are available. Set "type" to one of:
mcq      multiple choice          questions[] with prompt, options[], answer, explanation
reading  passage + questions      passage[], passageTitle, then questions[] as for mcq
gap      fill in the blank        questions[] with sentence (use ____ for the space),
answer (a word, or a list of acceptable words), hint
order    put parts in order       questions[] with prompt, parts[] IN THE CORRECT ORDER
(the website shuffles them for the student)
match    match word to meaning    pairs[] with term and meaning
error    correct the mistake      questions[] with sentence, answer (the corrected
sentence, or a list of acceptable versions), explanation
'answer' in mcq and reading is the POSITION of the correct option, counting
from 0. So 0 is the first option, 1 the second, 2 the third, 3 the fourth.
'page' tells site search which page the activity lives on.
Every activity automatically gets instructions, immediate feedback, a score
and a 'Start again' button. Nothing a student types is stored or sent anywhere.
After editing this file, run build.cmd.

activities.title: Grade 6: reading a timetable
activities.description: Competency levels 3.1 and 3.2 (2026 syllabus): reads a simple functional text related to real life, extracts the information conveyed and uses it appropriately.
activities.keywords: grade 6 english reading functional text timetable competency 3.1 3.2
activities.passageTitle: Bus times from Kandy to Matale
passage: MORNING BUSES - KANDY TO MATALE
Bus 593 leaves at 6.30 a.m. and arrives at 7.15 a.m.
Bus 594 leaves at 7.00 a.m. and arrives at 7.50 a.m.
Bus 596 leaves at 8.15 a.m. and arrives at 9.10 a.m.
Note: Bus 594 does not run on Sundays.

questions.prompt: Which bus takes the longest time to reach Matale?
options: They all take the same time
questions.explanation: Bus 596 leaves at 8.15 and arrives at 9.10, which is 55 minutes. Bus 593 takes 45 minutes and Bus 594 takes 50 minutes.

questions.prompt: It is Sunday morning. Nimali must be in Matale by 8.00 a.m. Which bus should she take?
options: No bus can get her there in time
questions.explanation: Bus 594 does not run on Sundays, and Bus 596 arrives too late. Bus 593 arrives at 7.15 a.m.

questions.prompt: How many buses leave Kandy before 8.00 a.m.?
questions.explanation: Bus 593 leaves at 6.30 and Bus 594 at 7.00. Bus 596 leaves at 8.15, which is after 8.00.

questions.prompt: Where would you most likely see a text like this?
options: In a letter to a friend
questions.explanation: A timetable is a functional text. It gives information people need in order to do something, so it is displayed where travellers will see it.

activities.title: Grade 6: filling in a form
activities.description: Competency level 4.1 (2026 syllabus): writes simple texts to convey information to fulfil the needs of immediacy in personal and official contexts, using forms with limited titles.
activities.keywords: grade 6 english form filling personal information competency 4.1 4.3

questions.sentence: A form asks for your ____ name. This is the name your family shares.
questions.hint: It is the name that comes last in Sri Lankan school registers.

questions.sentence: Date of ____: 14th March 2014.
questions.hint: The day you were born.

questions.sentence: The form asks for your ____ number so the school can telephone your home.
questions.hint: Something the school can call.

questions.sentence: Under ____, you would write: 15 Temple Road, Gampaha.
questions.hint: Where you live.

questions.sentence: Write a ____ of five things you need for school tomorrow.
questions.hint: Items written one under the other.

questions.sentence: Name with ____: R. M. Perera.
questions.hint: The first letters of your other names.

activities.title: Grade 6: reading a simple poem
activities.description: Competency levels 3.5 and 3.6 (2026 syllabus): reads a simple literary text, extracts the information conveyed and uses it appropriately. Poems of 4 to 16 lines on topics of interest.
activities.keywords: grade 6 english poem literary text rhyme competency 3.5 3.6 5.2
passage: The old rain tree beside our gate
Has stood there since before I came.
It holds the sunlight like a plate
And whispers something like my name.
When heavy clouds begin to break
And every road becomes a stream,
Its wide green arms are all I take
To keep me dry, and let me dream.

questions.prompt: Which two words at the ends of lines rhyme with each other?
questions.explanation: Came and name rhyme. So do gate and plate, and break and take.

questions.prompt: How does the poet use the tree when it rains?
options: To climb up and escape the water
To collect rainwater in a plate
questions.explanation: The poet says the tree's wide green arms keep him dry.

questions.prompt: The poem says the tree has 'wide green arms'. What does it really mean?
options: The tree's branches spread out widely
Someone is standing in the tree
questions.explanation: Arms is used to describe the branches. The poet writes about the tree as if it were a person.

questions.prompt: How does the poet feel about the tree?
questions.explanation: The tree whispers something like his name and shelters him. These are warm, friendly ideas.

activities.title: Grade 7: past continuous and future continuous
activities.description: Competency level 6.1: constructs simple sentences using the past continuous form and the future continuous form (Grade 7, Term 2).
activities.keywords: grade 7 english past continuous future continuous tense competency 6.1

questions.sentence: At six o'clock yesterday evening, Amali ____ (study) for her test.
questions.hint: One person, in the past, and the action was going on at that time.

questions.sentence: The children ____ (play) in the garden when it started to rain.
questions.hint: More than one child, so use were.

questions.sentence: This time tomorrow, we ____ (travel) to Nuwara Eliya.
questions.hint: An action that will be going on at a time in the future.

questions.sentence: I ____ (not listen) when the teacher gave the instructions.
questions.hint: Put not between was and the -ing word.

questions.sentence: Were you ____ (wait) for the bus when I saw you?
questions.hint: After Were you, use only the -ing word.

questions.sentence: Next Monday at nine, the students ____ (sit) the term test.
questions.hint: Future continuous: will be plus the -ing word.

activities.title: Grade 7: using modals
activities.description: Competency level 6.3: uses modals meaningfully, limited to can, would, must and should (Grade 7, Term 2).
activities.keywords: grade 7 english modals can would must should competency 6.3

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: 'You ____ wear your helmet. It is the law.'
questions.explanation: Must is used when something is necessary or required. A law leaves no choice.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: 'Ravi ____ swim very well. He learnt when he was five.'
questions.explanation: Can shows ability, that is, something a person is able to do.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: 'You look tired. You ____ go to bed early tonight.'
questions.explanation: Should gives advice. It is a suggestion, not an order.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: '____ you please pass me the dictionary?'
questions.explanation: Would you please is a polite way of asking someone to do something.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the modal correctly?
options: She must to finish her homework.
questions.explanation: A modal is followed by the plain form of the verb, with no to, no -ing and no -s.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: 'It is raining hard. We ____ take an umbrella.'
questions.explanation: Should is the sensible advice here. There is no law forcing them, but it is wise.

activities.title: Grade 7: joining words
activities.description: Competency level 6.8: uses conjunctions appropriately, limited to and, but, or, while, when, after, before and because (Grade 7, Term 2).
activities.keywords: grade 7 english conjunctions joining words because while competency 6.8

questions.sentence: I wanted to play cricket, ____ it began to rain.
questions.hint: The second part is the opposite of what you expected.

questions.sentence: We stayed at home ____ the roads were flooded.
questions.hint: It gives the reason.

questions.sentence: Wash your hands ____ you eat.
questions.hint: Washing comes first, eating comes second.

questions.sentence: My mother was cooking ____ I was doing my homework.
questions.hint: Two actions going on at the same time.

questions.sentence: Would you like tea ____ coffee?
questions.hint: A choice between two things.

questions.sentence: ____ the bell rang, all the children ran out.
questions.hint: It tells you the time that something happened.

activities.title: Grade 8: the past perfect tense
activities.description: Competency level 6.1: constructs simple sentences using the past perfect form, in positive, negative, positive question and negative question forms (Grade 8, Term 2).
activities.keywords: grade 8 english past perfect tense had competency 6.1

questions.sentence: When we reached the hall, the concert ____ (already begin).
questions.hint: It began first, then we reached. Use had plus the third form of the verb.

questions.sentence: Sunil ____ (not finish) his homework before the teacher came.
questions.hint: Put not between had and the third form.

questions.sentence: Had you ____ (eat) before you left home?
questions.hint: After Had you, use the third form of eat.

questions.sentence: She could not enter because she ____ (lose) her ticket.
questions.hint: Losing the ticket happened before she could not enter.

questions.sentence: By the time the bus arrived, everyone ____ (go) home.
questions.hint: The third form of go is gone.

questions.sentence: I did not recognise him because I ____ (never meet) him before.
questions.hint: Never goes between had and the third form.

activities.title: Grade 8: the passive voice in simple tenses
activities.description: Competency level 6.1: constructs simple sentences in the passive voice in the simple present, simple past and simple future (Grade 8, Terms 2 and 3).
activities.keywords: grade 8 english passive voice simple present past future competency 6.1

questions.sentence: The classroom is clean by the students every morning.
answer: The classroom is cleaned by the students every morning.
questions.explanation: The passive needs the third form of the verb. Clean becomes cleaned after is.

questions.sentence: The letters was posted yesterday.
questions.explanation: Letters is plural, so the verb must be were, not was.

questions.sentence: This bridge was build in 1962.
questions.explanation: The third form of build is built, not build.

questions.sentence: The results will announced next week.
answer: The results will be announced next week.
questions.explanation: The future passive is will be plus the third form. The word be is missing.

questions.sentence: Rice is grow in many parts of Sri Lanka.
answer: Rice is grown in many parts of Sri Lanka.
questions.explanation: The third form of grow is grown.

questions.sentence: The windows was broken by the storm.
answer: The windows were broken by the storm.
questions.explanation: Windows is plural, so use were.

activities.title: Grade 8: reflexive pronouns
activities.description: Competency level 6.2: uses pronouns appropriately, with reflexive pronouns introduced in Grade 8, Term 1.
activities.keywords: grade 8 english reflexive pronouns myself yourself competency 6.2

questions.sentence: I cut ____ while I was slicing the mango.
questions.hint: The person who did it and the person hurt are the same: I.

questions.sentence: The little boy dressed ____ without any help.
questions.hint: One boy.

questions.sentence: We enjoyed ____ at the school concert.
questions.hint: More than one person, and the word is we.

questions.sentence: Nadeesha wrote the whole essay ____.
questions.hint: One girl, and it means with nobody's help.

questions.sentence: Be careful, children, or you will hurt ____.
questions.hint: More than one person being spoken to.

questions.sentence: The cat washed ____ in the sunlight.
questions.hint: An animal or thing, not a person.

activities.title: Grade 9: passive voice, past and future
activities.description: Competency level 6.1: constructs simple sentences in the passive voice in the past tense and the future tense, in affirmative, negative and interrogative forms (Grade 9, Term 2).
activities.keywords: grade 9 english passive voice past future competency 6.1

questions.sentence: Change to the passive: 'The gardener planted these trees.' These trees ____ by the gardener.
questions.hint: Trees is plural and the time is past.

questions.sentence: Change to the passive: 'They will repair the road.' The road ____ soon.
questions.hint: Future passive: will be plus the third form.

questions.sentence: Change to the passive: 'Someone stole my bicycle.' My bicycle ____ last night.
questions.hint: The third form of steal is stolen.

questions.sentence: The prizes will not be ____ (give) today.
questions.hint: The third form of give.

questions.sentence: ____ the letters posted yesterday?
questions.hint: Letters is plural and the time is past.

questions.sentence: Change to the passive: 'The principal will open the new library.' The new library ____ by the principal.
questions.hint: Will be plus the third form of open.

activities.title: Grade 9: reported speech, statements
activities.description: Competency level 6.11: uses reported speech accurately, beginning with reported statements (Grade 9, Term 3).
activities.keywords: grade 9 english reported speech indirect statements competency 6.11

questions.sentence: He said that he is very tired.
answer: He said that he was very tired.
questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past, the present tense moves back to the past. Is becomes was.

questions.sentence: She told that she had finished her work.
answer: She said that she had finished her work.
She told me that she had finished her work.
questions.explanation: Told must be followed by a person. Use said that, or told me that.

questions.sentence: They said that they will come tomorrow.
answer: They said that they would come the next day.
They said that they would come the following day.
questions.explanation: Will becomes would, and tomorrow becomes the next day in reported speech.

questions.sentence: The teacher said that the earth was round.
answer: The teacher said that the earth is round.
questions.explanation: A fact that is always true keeps the present tense, even after a past reporting verb.

questions.sentence: Amara said that she can swim across the river.
answer: Amara said that she could swim across the river.
questions.explanation: Can becomes could in reported speech.

questions.sentence: He said that he saw her yesterday.
answer: He said that he had seen her the day before.
questions.explanation: The simple past moves back to the past perfect, and yesterday becomes the day before.

activities.title: Grade 9: reading between the lines
activities.description: Competency levels 5.7 and 5.8: infers ellipted information and infers implied information (Grade 9, Terms 2 and 3).
activities.keywords: grade 9 english inference implied information reading competency 5.7 5.8
passage: Kumari arrived at the classroom before anyone else, as she always did. She set her bag down and looked at the desk by the window. The chair was still pushed in, exactly as it had been on Monday, and on Tuesday, and on every day since.
She took out her books and arranged them slowly. When the others came in, laughing about a cricket match, nobody looked at the window.
At the interval, Miss Fernando called her aside. 'You may move to the front if you would like,' she said gently. Kumari shook her head.
'She might come back,' Kumari said.

questions.prompt: What can you work out about the person who sat by the window?
options: She has moved to the front of the class
She has been absent for several days
She is late that morning only
questions.explanation: The chair has been pushed in since Monday and on every day since. That tells us she has been away for some time, without the writer saying so.

questions.prompt: Why does Miss Fernando offer Kumari a seat at the front?
options: Miss Fernando thinks Kumari is lonely
questions.explanation: She speaks gently and offers a change. The kindness suggests she has noticed Kumari sitting alone beside an empty desk.

questions.prompt: What does Kumari's answer tell you about how she feels?
options: She is angry with her friend
She is still hoping her friend will return
She does not care where she sits
questions.explanation: 'She might come back' shows hope. Kumari refuses to move because moving would mean giving that hope up.

questions.prompt: The others came in 'laughing about a cricket match'. Why has the writer included this?
options: To show the match was important
To show the others enjoy cricket
To contrast their cheerfulness with Kumari's mood
To explain why the class was late
questions.explanation: Their laughter sits beside Kumari's quietness. The contrast makes her feeling stand out, without the writer naming it.

activities.title: Grade 10: passive voice in perfect and continuous forms
activities.description: Competency level 6.1: constructs sentences in the passive voice in the present and past continuous, and the present, past and future perfect (Grade 10, Terms 1, 2 and 3).
activities.keywords: grade 10 english passive voice perfect continuous competency 6.1

questions.sentence: Present perfect passive: The report ____ (complete) by the committee.
questions.hint: Has been plus the third form.

questions.sentence: Past perfect passive: The tickets ____ (sell) before we arrived.
questions.hint: Had been plus the third form.

questions.sentence: Present continuous passive: The road ____ (widen) at the moment.
questions.hint: Is being plus the third form.

questions.sentence: Past continuous passive: The house ____ (paint) when I visited.
questions.hint: Was being plus the third form.

questions.sentence: Future perfect passive: By December the work ____ (finish).
questions.hint: Will have been plus the third form.

questions.sentence: Present perfect passive: Many trees ____ (cut) down in this area.
questions.hint: Trees is plural, so use have been.

activities.title: Grade 10: If Type 3
activities.description: Competency level 6.10: identifies 'If' Type 3, the conditional used for things that did not happen (Grade 10, Term 3).
activities.keywords: grade 10 english conditional if type 3 third conditional competency 6.10

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If I ____ harder, I would have passed the examination.'
questions.explanation: Type 3 uses if plus the past perfect: if I had studied.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If she had left earlier, she ____ the train.'
questions.explanation: The second half of a Type 3 sentence uses would have plus the third form.

questions.prompt: What does 'If we had known, we would have helped' tell you?
options: They did not know, so they did not help
They will know and will help
They know but will not help
questions.explanation: Type 3 describes the opposite of what really happened. They did not know, so no help was given.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a correct Type 3 conditional?
options: If he had come, I would tell him.
If he came, I would have told him.
If he had come, I would have told him.
If he comes, I would have told him.
questions.explanation: Type 3 needs the past perfect after if, and would have plus the third form in the other half.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If the driver had not braked, there ____ an accident.'
questions.explanation: Would have been is the Type 3 form. The accident did not in fact happen.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a Type 3 sentence?
options: If I had seen you, I would have waved.
If it had rained, the match would have stopped.
If you had asked, I would have agreed.
If you ask, I will agree.
questions.explanation: The last one is Type 1. It uses the present tense and will, and describes something still possible.

activities.title: Grade 10: discourse markers
activities.description: Competency level 3.7: recognizes discourse markers, the words and phrases that signal how ideas connect (Grade 10, Term 3).
activities.keywords: grade 10 english discourse markers however therefore linking words competency 3.7

questions.sentence: The scheme was expensive. ____, it saved many lives.
questions.hint: The second idea contrasts with the first.

questions.sentence: It rained heavily all week. ____, the match was cancelled.
questions.hint: The second idea is the result of the first.

questions.sentence: ____, I would like to thank the principal for inviting me.
questions.hint: It signals the first point in a speech.

questions.sentence: The soil here is poor. ____, there is very little rainfall.
questions.hint: It adds a second, similar point.

questions.sentence: ____, the project succeeded because the villagers themselves ran it.
questions.hint: It signals the last point, summing up.

questions.sentence: Some students prefer science. ____ the other hand, others are drawn to the arts.
questions.hint: The phrase is on the other hand.

activities.title: Grade 11: conditional clauses
activities.description: Competency level 6.10: uses the conditional clauses appropriately, covering Types 1, 2 and 3 together (Grade 11, Term 1).
activities.keywords: grade 11 english conditionals if clauses type 1 2 3 competency 6.10

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If it rains tomorrow, we ____ the trip.'
questions.explanation: Type 1 describes something that may really happen: if plus the present, then will plus the plain verb.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If I ____ the President, I would change the education system.'
questions.explanation: Type 2 imagines something untrue now. Were is used with all subjects in this pattern.

questions.prompt: Which type is this? 'If she had studied medicine, she would have become a doctor.'
questions.explanation: Past perfect after if, and would have plus the third form. That is Type 3, about something that did not happen.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If you heat water to 100 degrees, it ____.'
questions.explanation: For something always true, both halves use the present tense. This is sometimes called the zero conditional.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: If I will see him, I will tell him.
If I see him, I will tell him.
If I saw him, I will tell him.
If I had seen him, I will tell him.
questions.explanation: Will is not used after if in a Type 1 sentence. The if half takes the present tense.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If we had left on time, we ____ stuck in this traffic now.'
questions.explanation: The if half is Type 3 but the result is about now, so it takes would not be. Mixed conditionals like this appear at Grade 11.

activities.title: Grade 11: reported questions and commands
activities.description: Competency level 6.11: uses reported speech accurately, extended to reported questions, commands and requests (Grade 11, Term 1).
activities.keywords: grade 11 english reported speech questions commands requests competency 6.11

questions.sentence: He asked me where did I live.
answer: He asked me where I lived.
questions.explanation: A reported question takes normal word order, not question order. Did disappears and the verb moves to the past.

questions.sentence: She asked me that I was ready.
answer: She asked me if I was ready.
She asked me whether I was ready.
questions.explanation: A yes or no question is reported with if or whether, never with that.

questions.sentence: The teacher told us open our books.
answer: The teacher told us to open our books.
questions.explanation: A reported command uses told plus a person plus to plus the verb.

questions.sentence: He asked me what was my name.
answer: He asked me what my name was.
questions.explanation: In a reported question the subject comes before the verb: what my name was.

questions.sentence: She requested me don't tell anyone.
answer: She requested me not to tell anyone.
She asked me not to tell anyone.
questions.explanation: A negative request is reported with not to plus the plain verb.

questions.sentence: The officer asked him why he has come late.
answer: The officer asked him why he had come late.
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, the present perfect moves back to the past perfect.

activities.title: Grade 11: affixes and word class
activities.description: Competency levels 4.4 and 4.7: uses affixes to change the word class and the meaning of words, and uses nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs appropriately (Grade 11, Term 1).
activities.keywords: grade 11 english affixes prefixes suffixes word class competency 4.4 4.7

pairs.meaning: the noun formed from the adjective strong
the verb meaning to make stronger
the adjective formed from the noun success
the adverb telling you how something was done
the opposite of necessary, formed with a prefix
the noun meaning a failure to agree
the noun formed from careless
the verb meaning to understand wrongly

activities.title: Tenses: choosing the right form
activities.description: Ten questions on the tenses most often tested at Ordinary Level.
activities.keywords: tenses present past perfect continuous grammar quiz

questions.prompt: Nimal ____ to school every day.
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for a habit. With he, she or it, the verb takes -s: Nimal goes.

questions.prompt: Look! The bus ____ .
questions.explanation: The present continuous describes something happening at this moment. The word Look! tells you it is happening now.

questions.prompt: I ____ my homework already, so I can play now.
questions.explanation: The present perfect joins a past action to the present. The word already is a common signal for it.

questions.prompt: While I ____ , the telephone rang.
questions.explanation: Use the past continuous for the longer action that was already going on, and the simple past for the shorter action that interrupted it.

questions.prompt: She ____ in Kandy since 2015.
questions.explanation: Since names a starting point in the past and the situation continues, so the present perfect is used.

questions.prompt: We ____ the museum last Friday.
questions.explanation: Last Friday is a finished time, so the simple past is correct. Do not use the present perfect with a finished time expression.

questions.prompt: By the time we arrived, the film ____ .
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows which of two past actions happened first. The film started before you arrived.

questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ the match.
questions.explanation: In the first conditional the if-clause uses the simple present and the main clause uses will.

questions.prompt: The results ____ next week.
questions.explanation: The results do not announce anything; something is done to them, so the passive will be announced is needed.

questions.prompt: He ____ television when his father came home.
questions.explanation: The past continuous describes the action in progress; the simple past came describes the shorter action that broke into it.

activities.title: Prepositions: in, on, at and the rest
activities.description: Eight questions on prepositions of time, place and movement.
activities.keywords: prepositions in on at grammar quiz

questions.prompt: The examination begins ____ 8.30 in the morning.
questions.explanation: Use at with a clock time: at 8.30, at noon, at midnight.

questions.prompt: My birthday is ____ May.
questions.explanation: Use in with months, seasons and years: in May, in December, in 2026.

questions.prompt: We have a test ____ Monday.
questions.explanation: Use on with days and dates: on Monday, on 15 March.

questions.prompt: She is very good ____ mathematics.
questions.explanation: Good at is a fixed pairing. We say good at a subject or a skill.

questions.prompt: Please listen ____ the instructions carefully.
questions.explanation: Listen is followed by to when there is an object: listen to the teacher, listen to music.

questions.prompt: The book is ____ the shelf.
questions.explanation: Use on for a surface. The shelf is a flat surface, so the book rests on it.

questions.prompt: He has been waiting ____ two hours.
questions.explanation: Use for with a length of time (for two hours) and since with a starting point (since ten o'clock).

questions.prompt: I apologised ____ being late.
questions.explanation: Apologise for is the usual pairing: apologise for a mistake, apologise for being late.

activities.title: Articles: a, an and the
activities.description: Type the missing article in each space.
activities.keywords: articles a an the fill in the blank

questions.sentence: My father is ____ engineer.
questions.hint: The next word begins with a vowel sound.
questions.explanation: Use an before a vowel sound: an engineer, an hour, an umbrella.

questions.sentence: She bought ____ new bicycle yesterday.
questions.explanation: Use a before a consonant sound, and when the thing is mentioned for the first time.

questions.sentence: ____ sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: Use the before something there is only one of, such as the sun, the moon and the sky.

questions.sentence: I waited for ____ hour at the bus stand.
questions.hint: Listen to the sound, not the letter.
questions.explanation: Hour begins with the letter h, but the h is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound and takes an.

questions.sentence: He is ____ most careful student in the class.
questions.explanation: Superlatives take the: the most careful, the best, the tallest.

questions.sentence: We saw ____ elephant near the tank.
questions.explanation: Elephant begins with a vowel sound, so an is used.

questions.sentence: Colombo is ____ capital of Sri Lanka.
questions.explanation: There is only one capital, so the is used.

questions.sentence: Would you like ____ cup of tea?
questions.explanation: One of several cups, mentioned for the first time, so a is correct.

activities.title: Verb forms: putting the verb in the right shape
activities.description: Write the correct form of the verb given in brackets.
activities.keywords: verb forms tenses fill in the blank practice

questions.sentence: The children ____ (play) in the garden now.
questions.hint: Something happening at this moment.
questions.explanation: The word now signals the present continuous: are playing.

questions.sentence: Water ____ (boil) at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: A general truth takes the simple present. With water (it), the verb takes -s.

questions.sentence: I ____ (not see) him since Tuesday.
questions.explanation: Since points to a starting time and the situation continues, so the present perfect is used.

questions.sentence: They ____ (finish) the work before the rain started.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the action that happened first of two past actions.

questions.sentence: The letter ____ (write) by the principal.
questions.explanation: The letter did not write anything, so the passive is needed: was written by the principal.

questions.sentence: She enjoys ____ (read) detective stories.
questions.explanation: After enjoy, the verb takes the -ing form: enjoy reading, enjoy swimming.

activities.title: Sentence ordering: building a correct sentence
activities.description: Put the parts in the right order to make a correct English sentence.
activities.keywords: sentence order word order syntax activity

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: English usually follows subject, verb, object or place, then time.

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Already comes between the auxiliary verb has and the main verb informed.

questions.prompt: Make a correct question:

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: A sentence that begins with although needs a complete main clause after the comma.

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: In the first conditional the if-clause comes first, followed by a comma and the will-clause.

activities.title: Reading comprehension: The village library
activities.description: Read the passage, then answer the six questions. This is the kind of passage used in Paper I.
activities.keywords: reading comprehension passage questions practice
passage: For many years the small village of Weliketiya had no library of its own. The nearest one was in the town, eleven kilometres away, and the bus that went there ran only twice a day. Children who wanted a book to read outside their school textbooks had to depend on the few volumes their teachers were able to lend them.

In 2019 a retired postmaster named Mr Alwis offered the front room of his house to the village. He had a large table, four chairs and, most importantly, patience. Villagers were asked to give any books they could spare. Within three months more than six hundred books had been collected, and the room was opened every evening from four o'clock until seven.

The library was not run by anybody official. Mr Alwis kept a simple notebook in which borrowers wrote their name, the title of the book and the date. There were no fines. If a book came back late, he said nothing; if it did not come back at all, he wrote the title on a separate page and hoped that one day it would return. Surprisingly, most books did.

What changed the village was not the number of books but the habit. Children who had never owned a story book began to read one every week. Parents who had left school early came in the evenings and borrowed simple books in English. Two of the older students began reading aloud to the youngest children on Saturday mornings, and that arrangement continues today.

questions.prompt: Before 2019, why was it difficult for the children of Weliketiya to borrow books?
options: The village library was closed for repairs.
The nearest library was far away and the bus was infrequent.
The children were not allowed to join the town library.
Their teachers refused to lend them books.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says the nearest library was eleven kilometres away and the bus ran only twice a day.

questions.prompt: What did Mr Alwis give to the village?
options: Six hundred books from his own collection
Money to build a library building
The front room of his house, and his time
A bus service to the town library
questions.explanation: He offered the front room of his house, together with a table, chairs and patience. The books came from the villagers.

questions.prompt: How were the books collected?
options: They were bought with money raised in the village.
They were sent by the town library.
Villagers gave books they could spare.
The school donated its old textbooks.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph states that villagers were asked to give any books they could spare.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about Mr Alwis's way of running the library?
options: It was strict and carefully controlled.
It was unpopular with the villagers.
questions.explanation: There were no fines, records were kept in a simple notebook, and late books were met with silence. This shows a trusting, informal manner.

questions.prompt: According to the last paragraph, what mattered most about the library?
options: The money it saved the village
The fact that it was free
questions.explanation: The writer says plainly that what changed the village was not the number of books but the habit.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means 'happening or existing without an official arrangement'?
questions.explanation: Informal is the word that matches this meaning. The passage tells us the library was not run by anybody official.

activities.title: Literature: naming the technique
activities.description: Eight questions asking you to name the technique a writer has used. Naming the technique correctly is the first step in every good Literature answer.
activities.keywords: literary techniques simile metaphor quiz literature

questions.prompt: 'The classroom was as quiet as a temple at dawn.' Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: The comparison uses the word as, so it is a simile. A metaphor would say the classroom was a temple.

questions.prompt: 'The wind pushed open the door and walked into the room.' Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: The wind is given the human actions of pushing and walking, so this is personification.

questions.prompt: 'Silent shadows slipped across the sand.' Which technique is most obvious?
questions.explanation: The s sound is repeated at the start of several nearby words, which is alliteration.

questions.prompt: A fire officer's own house burns down. In literary terms this is an example of:
questions.explanation: There is a sharp contrast between what we would expect and what actually happens, which is irony.

questions.prompt: A character alone on stage speaks his private thoughts aloud to the audience. This is a:
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is spoken by a character who is alone, revealing thoughts the other characters do not hear.

questions.prompt: 'Her hands were rough maps of forty harvests.' Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: The hands are spoken of as though they actually were maps, with no like or as, so it is a metaphor.

questions.prompt: In a story, a broken watch that the father keeps for thirty years stands for time that cannot be recovered. The watch is being used as a:
questions.explanation: An object that stands for a larger idea beyond itself is a symbol.

questions.prompt: Which of these best defines a theme?
options: The order in which events happen
The place where the story is set
A central idea about life that the work explores
questions.explanation: A theme is an idea about life, such as loss, duty or the cost of ambition. The order of events is plot; the place is setting; the person telling it is the narrator.

activities.title: Error correction: find the mistake and put it right
activities.description: Each sentence has one mistake. Rewrite the whole sentence correctly.
activities.keywords: error correction common mistakes grammar editing

questions.sentence: She don't like cold weather.
answer: She does not like cold weather
questions.explanation: With he, she or it, the negative is doesn't, not don't.

questions.sentence: I am living here since 2018.
answer: I have been living here since 2018
questions.explanation: Since with a continuing situation needs the present perfect, not the present continuous.

questions.sentence: He is more taller than his brother.
answer: He is taller than his brother
questions.explanation: Do not use more together with an -er comparative. Taller is already the comparative form.

questions.sentence: The informations you gave me were useful.
answer: The information you gave me was useful
The information you gave me was very useful
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable. It has no plural and takes a singular verb.

questions.sentence: We discussed about the problem yesterday.
questions.explanation: Discuss is followed directly by its object. Do not add about.

questions.sentence: Every students must bring a pen.
answer: Every student must bring a pen
questions.explanation: Every is followed by a singular noun: every student, every day, every question.

questions.sentence: He asked me where do I live.
answer: He asked me where I live
He asked me where I lived
questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order returns to normal statement order, and do is dropped.

questions.sentence: I look forward to hear from you.
answer: I look forward to hearing from you
questions.explanation: In look forward to, the word to is a preposition, so the verb after it takes the -ing form.

activities.title: Letter sounds: which sound does the word begin with?
activities.description: Ten questions on the first sound of a word. For children who are learning to sound out.
activities.keywords: letter sounds phonics first sound alphabet primary beginners

questions.prompt: Which sound does the word 'sun' begin with?
questions.explanation: Sun begins with the s sound. The letter c can also make an s sound, but sun is spelt with s.

questions.prompt: Which sound does the word 'mango' begin with?
questions.explanation: Mango begins with m. Put your lips together and hum: mmm.

questions.prompt: Which sound does the word 'kite' begin with?
questions.explanation: Kite begins with k. The letter c makes the same sound in cat.

questions.prompt: Which sound does the word 'elephant' begin with?
questions.explanation: Elephant begins with the short e sound, as in egg.

questions.prompt: Which word begins with the same sound as 'dog'?
questions.explanation: Door and dog both begin with d. Goat begins with g, which is a different sound.

questions.prompt: Which word begins with the same sound as 'fish'?
questions.explanation: Five begins with f, like fish. Phone also sounds like f, but it is spelt with ph, which comes later.

questions.prompt: Which sound does the word 'tree' begin with?
questions.explanation: Tree begins with t. The r comes second, so you hear t-r at the start.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT begin with the b sound?
questions.explanation: Day begins with d. Remember that b and d face opposite ways.

questions.prompt: Which sound does the word 'rain' begin with?
questions.explanation: Rain begins with r.

questions.prompt: Which word begins with the same sound as 'pen'?
questions.explanation: Paper begins with p, like pen. Ball begins with b, which is made in the same place in the mouth but with your voice on.

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'night'?

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'moon'?

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'boat'?

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'star'?

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'rain'?
questions.explanation: Rain and train both end with the -ain sound.

questions.prompt: Which two words rhyme: bell, ball, well?
questions.explanation: Bell and well both end with the -ell sound. Ball has a different middle sound.

activities.title: Reading: The mango tree
activities.description: A short passage with six questions. Read it twice before you begin.
activities.keywords: reading comprehension primary short passage children questions
passage: There was an old mango tree behind our house. It was taller than the roof, and its branches came right up to my bedroom window.

Every April the tree was full of mangoes, and every April the crows got there before we did. Thatha said we should pick them early, while they were still a little green. I wanted to wait until they were sweet.
One morning I woke up and counted eleven crows on the branches. By the evening there were no mangoes left at all.
The next year I picked them early.

questions.prompt: Where was the mango tree?
options: In the garden of the school
questions.explanation: The first sentence says the tree was behind our house.

questions.prompt: How do we know the tree was very tall?
options: It was older than the house
It was taller than the roof
It gave a lot of shade
questions.explanation: The passage says it was taller than the roof, and its branches reached the bedroom window.

questions.prompt: In which month was the tree full of mangoes?
questions.explanation: The passage says every April the tree was full of mangoes.

questions.prompt: What did Thatha want to do?
questions.explanation: Thatha said they should pick them early, while they were still a little green.

questions.prompt: How many crows did the writer count?
questions.explanation: The writer counted eleven crows on the branches that morning.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer pick the mangoes early the next year?
options: Because the mangoes tasted better green
Because Thatha told them to again
Because the crows had eaten them all the year before
Because the tree was cut down
questions.explanation: The crows ate every mango in one day, so the following year the writer took Thatha's advice.

activities.title: Grade 5 Scholarship: English language practice
activities.description: Twelve questions of the kind that test English in the English-medium paper: vocabulary, opposites, categories, analogies and grammar in use.
activities.keywords: grade 5 scholarship English practice verbal reasoning opposites analogies vocabulary

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'enormous'.
questions.explanation: Enormous means very big, so huge is closest. Heavy is about weight, not size.

questions.prompt: Choose the opposite of 'ancient'.
questions.explanation: Ancient means very old, so its opposite is modern.

questions.prompt: Which is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Rose, jasmine and orchid are flowers. Mango is a fruit.

questions.prompt: Hand is to glove as foot is to ___.
questions.explanation: A glove goes on a hand, so a shoe goes on a foot. Say the relationship aloud first.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The two brothers helped ___ with the work.
questions.explanation: Each other is used when there are two people. One another is generally used for more than two.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.explanation: A sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. Market is a common noun, so it does not need a capital.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'exhausted'.
questions.explanation: Exhausted means extremely tired.

questions.prompt: Which is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Train, bus and aeroplane carry people. A road is the place you travel on, not a vehicle.

questions.prompt: Doctor is to hospital as teacher is to ___.
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital, so a teacher works in a school. The relationship is person to workplace.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: There ___ five books on the table.
questions.explanation: Five books is plural, so the verb is are.

questions.prompt: Choose the opposite of 'generous'.
questions.explanation: A generous person gives freely; a selfish person does not. Poor is about money, not willingness.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence best? The road was so ___ that only one car could pass at a time.
questions.explanation: Only one car being able to pass tells you the road was narrow. Read the whole sentence with your answer in it to check.
